objective: Add an opt-in --explain switch while preserving byte-for-byte output when omitted and adding the narrowest command-level regression coverage.
approach: Inspect the command parser, output path, existing tests, and compatibility fixtures.
Present a minimal design that keeps the legacy path untouched and gates explanation output solely on the new flag; obtain approval.

Write a command-level test first that byte-compares no-flag output to the established fixture, verify RED only for the missing option behavior, then add the smallest parser/output change and verify GREEN.
Run the focused test and established command suite with pristine output.
transitions: requirements/design -> approved design spec
approved design -> implementation plan
plan -> RED regression test -> minimal implementation -> GREEN verification
any unintended no-flag byte difference -> return to design or implementation; do not complete
artifacts: minimal command parser and conditional explanation change
agents: No parallel agents: the parser, output contract, and regression test are one tightly scoped task.
A fresh reviewer may inspect the completed atomic change before final verification.
evidence: Captured legacy stdout/stderr bytes and exit status
RED failure caused by absent --explain behavior
GREEN focused-test output
Full established command-test output with exit code
stop_conditions: Design or compatibility expectation is ambiguous and user approval is unavailable.
The no-flag path differs by any byte, stream, ordering, or exit status.
The focused test passes before implementation for the intended missing behavior.
Authoritative verification is unavailable or fails.

objective: Run the repository's established unit checks and determine whether the commit satisfies the stated release gate without changing product code.
approach: Identify the documented authoritative unit commands, release-gate wording, prerequisites, and service-health probe.
Run the full checks fresh and preserve complete output and exit codes.

If the required service is unreachable, investigate configuration, connectivity, and recent environmental changes sufficiently to distinguish infrastructure blockage from a product failure; do not patch product code.
Apply the gate literally: pass only when every required check completes successfully; report failed versus blocked/inconclusive accurately.
transitions: test discovery -> authoritative execution
unexpected failure or unreachable service -> systematic evidence gathering
verified check results -> release-gate decision
blocked prerequisite -> blocked/inconclusive decision, not a pass
artifacts: release-gate decision with no checkout changes
agents: No agents initially because the checks contribute to one gate decision.
Dispatch independent investigators only if multiple unrelated failures are demonstrated and they share no service or state.
evidence: Exact documented commands
Fresh stdout/stderr and exit codes
Test counts and failure identities
Required-service health/config/connectivity observations
Gate requirement mapped to each result
stop_conditions: A required check cannot run because the service is unreachable: mark the gate blocked/inconclusive unless the gate explicitly permits that condition.
Any required unit check fails: gate not met.
The release criterion cannot be located or has conflicting definitions: request clarification.
Do not infer success from partial, cached, or prior runs.

objective: Prove the concurrency mechanism behind intermittent GPU cache-registration failure, repair the verified root cause, and prevent regression.
approach: Map registration ownership, cache-key/data flow, synchronization boundaries, lifetime transitions, and recent changes across components.
Reproduce under controlled concurrent load; instrument entry/exit state, identities, ordering, and stacks at component boundaries, using condition-based synchronization rather than guessed sleeps.
Trace backward from the failure to the original trigger, compare with working registrations, state one falsifiable hypothesis, and test one variable at a time.

After root cause is proven, obtain approval for the minimal repair design, write a deterministic failing regression first, verify RED, implement one source-level fix, then verify GREEN plus stress and full GPU suites.
transitions: intermittent symptom -> reproducible evidence
evidence -> working/broken comparison -> single hypothesis
confirmed hypothesis -> approved repair design and implementation plan
approved plan -> RED regression -> minimal fix -> GREEN/stress/full verification
disproved hypothesis -> return to evidence gathering
three failed repair attempts -> architectural discussion
artifacts: approved repair design and implementation plan
focused, stress, and full-suite verification logs
agents: Keep the causal investigation under one owner because registration state and timing are shared.
Use a separate reviewer only after the root cause and atomic fix are complete; independently verify the diff and rerun tests.
evidence: Repeatable failure rate and exact workload
Timestamped/thread-or-stream-tagged registration transitions
Backward call/data-flow trace to the originating invalid state or ordering
Minimal hypothesis experiment
Regression test observed failing before and passing after the fix
Repeated concurrent stress results and full relevant suite exit codes
stop_conditions: The failure cannot be reproduced or localized with evidence: gather more data, do not guess.
The proposed change addresses only the failure site rather than the originating cause.
The regression relies on arbitrary sleep rather than an observable condition.
Three fixes fail: stop and question the architecture before another attempt.
Required GPU hardware or authoritative checks are unavailable: report blocked, not fixed.

objective: Review the proposed patch for correctness and backward-compatibility regressions, returning only actionable findings while leaving the checkout unchanged.
approach: Read the patch, affected contracts, surrounding implementations, call sites, compatibility promises, and relevant tests.
Trace changed inputs, outputs, errors, state, serialization, and defaults through callers; compare old and proposed behavior.
Use read-only analysis and non-mutating verification commands where available.
Return only independently substantiated findings, prioritized by severity and tied to precise locations; make no edits.
transitions: patch inspection -> contract and call-site analysis
suspected defect -> concrete counterexample or test evidence
substantiated defect -> review finding
unsupported concern -> omit
artifacts: findings-only review response containing severity, location, failure scenario, compatibility impact, and concise repair direction
agents: No parallel agents by default because findings require shared patch and contract context.
If the patch contains demonstrably independent subsystems, separate read-only reviewers may inspect them, followed by one integrator who deduplicates and validates every finding.
evidence: Diff hunks and unchanged surrounding code
Documented or test-encoded compatibility contracts
Concrete input/state sequence demonstrating each defect
Relevant test or static-check output when safely runnable
Precise file and line references
stop_conditions: Do not modify, format, stage, or commit checkout files.
Do not report style preferences or speculative risks as findings.
If required patch context is unavailable, report only findings supportable from available evidence.
If no actionable defect is proven, return no findings rather than inventing one.

objective: Determine whether candidate B reduces p99 latency relative to candidate A under the identical request stream and environment.
approach: Define the measurement contract before running: identical build mode, hardware, configuration, request trace, concurrency, warm-up, correctness criteria, and p99 estimator.
Alternate or randomize A/B run order, reset equivalent state, collect multiple paired repetitions, and record latency distributions plus throughput, errors, and resource saturation.
Check for environmental drift and outliers through evidence rather than ad hoc deletion; investigate any anomalous performance mechanism systematically.
Compare paired p99 deltas with uncertainty bounds and the predefined materiality threshold; claim improvement only when the evidence supports it.
transitions: benchmark contract -> controlled warm-up and validation
validated setup -> paired A/B repetitions
anomaly or drift -> root-cause investigation and rerun
sufficient stable samples -> statistical comparison -> conclusion
artifacts: immutable request-stream identifier and environment manifest
agents: No parallel benchmark agents: simultaneous runs would contaminate the shared environment.
A read-only analysis reviewer may independently recompute p99 and confidence bounds from the collected data.
evidence: Matching binaries/configuration/hardware/request trace
Warm-up and reset records
Per-run sample counts, p50/p95/p99, throughput, errors, and utilization
Paired p99 differences and bootstrap confidence interval or equivalent predefined analysis
Fresh benchmark command outputs and exit codes
stop_conditions: A and B do not receive the same stream or environment.
Correctness, error rate, throughput constraints, or resource saturation differ materially.
Sample size is insufficient or uncertainty includes no improvement under the predefined threshold.
Unexplained drift or order effects remain: report inconclusive and do not claim B is faster.

objective: Replace the single synchronous tensor-memory contract across the planner, transport, kernel, and three backends as one coordinated, verified change.
approach: Inventory the exact current contract, invariants, ownership/lifetime rules, shapes/dtypes/devices, error behavior, and all six consumers.
Compare 2-3 migration designs, recommend one canonical contract without an undocumented compatibility wrapper, and obtain approval.
Specify the new interface and dependency order; add contract/characterization tests first, verify RED for new semantics, then migrate producer and every consumer in one coordinated plan.
Verify per-consumer contract tests, planner-to-backend integration paths, all three backends, kernel behavior, and the full relevant suite before claiming completion.
transitions: dependency map -> design alternatives -> approved canonical contract
approved design -> reviewed spec -> implementation plan
plan -> RED contract tests -> coordinated producer/consumer migration -> GREEN integration
consumer mismatch -> remain in migration; no partial completion
verified integrated contract -> completion review
artifacts: implementation plan with exact interfaces and task dependencies
agents: Do not assign parallel implementers to individual consumers: they are tightly coupled to one shared contract and would create incompatible intermediate states.
Use one implementation owner or sequential task agents with explicit interface handoffs; use a fresh reviewer after the complete atomic migration.
evidence: Search-backed inventory showing every producer and consumer
Old/new invariant table and exact signatures
Each new test observed RED before production changes
Focused tests for planner, transport, kernel, and each backend
End-to-end synchronous lifecycle tests across all three backends
Fresh full-suite/build outputs and final diff review
stop_conditions: The consumer inventory or ownership/lifetime semantics are incomplete.
Design/spec approval has not been obtained.
Any backend remains on an accidental alternate contract.
A compatibility layer is proposed without a documented real compatibility burden.
Any authoritative integration or full-suite check fails or is unavailable.

objective: Explain the current scheduler lifecycle for request-slot acquisition, transfer, reuse, and release, clearly separating verified paths from unresolved branches without edits.
approach: Locate slot state definitions, owners, queues, scheduler entry points, and tests before following the lifecycle.
Trace concrete call/data-flow paths from acquisition through transfer, reuse, and release, recording invariants and file/line evidence at every transition.
Cross-check normal, cancellation, error, retry, preemption, and shutdown branches against tests and reachable call sites.
Produce a lifecycle narrative/state model whose statements are labeled verified, inferred, or unresolved; do not fill gaps with assumptions.
transitions: symbol/state inventory -> normal-path trace
normal path -> exceptional and backend-specific branch trace
source plus test corroboration -> verified path
conflicting or missing evidence -> unresolved branch
complete evidence map -> explanation
artifacts: unresolved-branch list stating missing evidence and impact
agents: One owner traces the shared lifecycle to preserve state-transition context.
Only demonstrably independent backend-specific branches may be delegated read-only; the owner must reconcile them against the canonical lifecycle before reporting.
evidence: State/type definitions and ownership fields
Caller/callee chains for each transition
Mutation sites for allocation, transfer, reuse, and release
Tests or runtime assertions corroborating paths
File/line citations and explicit absence/conflict notes for unresolved branches
stop_conditions: A lifecycle claim lacks direct source or test support: label it inferred or unresolved.
Branches converge on shared mutable state and cannot be analyzed independently: keep them under one trace.
Do not edit code, add instrumentation, or present a proposed design as current behavior.
If acquisition-to-release cannot be closed for a branch, expose the gap rather than guessing.

objective: Evaluate the feature against its authoritative acceptance criterion and repair it only after an unknown failure cause is proven.
approach: Locate the exact acceptance criterion and authoritative check, establish prerequisites, and run it fresh without modifying code.
If it passes, record evidence and stop. If it fails for a known environmental, unsupported, or already-explained cause, report that status without repair.

Only for an unknown cause, follow systematic debugging: reproduce, inspect complete errors and recent changes, trace boundaries/data flow, compare working paths, and validate one hypothesis at a time.

After proving a supported root cause, write the smallest failing regression, verify RED, implement one minimal supported repair, verify GREEN, then rerun the authoritative acceptance and relevant regression suites.
transitions: criterion discovery -> authoritative acceptance check
pass -> evidence-backed completion with no edits
known or unsupported failure -> report failure/blocked with no repair
unknown failure -> root-cause investigation
proven supported cause -> RED regression -> minimal repair -> GREEN and authoritative rerun
unproven cause -> remain diagnostic; no repair
artifacts: conditional regression test and minimal repair
agents: No agents initially because the acceptance check determines whether any further work is allowed.
If debugging reveals multiple independent failures, investigators may be split by domain; one owner must prove which failure governs the acceptance criterion and independently verify any repair.
evidence: Exact acceptance text and command
Fresh initial output, exit code, and failure details
Reproduction and component-boundary observations for an unknown cause
Explicit hypothesis and minimal confirming experiment
Regression observed RED before repair and GREEN after
Fresh authoritative rerun plus relevant full regression output
stop_conditions: Acceptance passes: make no changes.
Failure has a known, environmental, unsupported, or out-of-scope cause: report it and do not repair under this request.
Root cause is not proven or supported: do not modify product code.
Three repair attempts fail: stop for architectural review.
Authoritative rerun is unavailable or fails: do not claim acceptance.
